GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
While language models can generate text continuations of any input, OpenAI's models have been fine-tuned on inputs formatted as conversations, consisting of lists of messages; in these conversations, the model is only designed to play one participant, called the assistant; in this document, 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - assistant_definition: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.
  - conversation_definition: A conversation is a list of messages, each containing a role and content; roles determine authority of instructions.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1_170_n066' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0116-L0116:
While language models can generate text continuations of any input, our models have been fine-tuned on inputs formatted as **conversations**, consisting of lists of **messages**. In these conversations, the model is only designed to play one participant, called the **assistant**. In this document, when we discuss model behavior, we're referring to its behavior as the assistant; "model" and "assistant" will be approximately synonymous.
